cards.title: Founder Story Scripting from Personal Problem Onward
cards.summary: A founder ad scripts the actual sequence of the founder's own problem, self-solutioning, material choices, and present-day proof.
cards.use_when: Structuring a long-form founder origin story for a product brand, even at large scale, and especially when AI-generated creative is flooding the feed.

cards.title: Match Ads to the Stages of Awareness
cards.summary: Place most creative in early awareness stages and roughly 20% at product/solution-aware stages, because a bottom-funnel ad cannot educate a cold audience.
cards.use_when: Allocating creative concepts across prospecting and retargeting campaigns, or diagnosing why an ad with good engagement isn't scaling.

cards.title: Founder Story Built on a Discovered Ingredient
cards.summary: A colostrum-gummies founder ad stacked a shocking hook, a family-transformation story, objective proof, and a manufacturing credibility reveal.
cards.use_when: Building acquisition creative for a supplement or ingestible brand with a novel delivery format.

cards.title: Sequencing Proof Before Product Reveal
cards.summary: A premium toothbrush ad front-loads a founder story and problem agitation and delays the product reveal, letting low-fi founder footage contrast with premium product shots.
cards.use_when: Creating acquisition video for a premium-positioned product where you want to justify the price before showing the product.

cards.title: Diagnose Bottom-Funnel-Only Creative Portfolios
cards.summary: An ad library built entirely on a founder's personal brand and late-stage objections cannot scale on cold audiences.
cards.use_when: Auditing a brand's existing creative library before scaling spend or when evaluating a celebrity/founder-fronted ad account's structure.

cards.title: Hook objective: qualify viewers, not just grab attention
cards.summary: A hook's job is to pull in relevant users at the right awareness stage so you can educate them, not to indiscriminately capture everyone.
cards.use_when: Writing or auditing the opening 3-5 seconds of a paid social video ad for a product page or direct-response campaign.

cards.title: Match the hook's awareness stage to the ad's body stage
cards.summary: A top-of-funnel hook running into a bottom-of-funnel product-tour body creates mismatched data and poor performance.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a video ad has high attention but low conversion on a store's Meta campaign.

cards.title: Write a bridge that delays the product pitch
cards.summary: The transition from hook to educational body is the 'bridge', and introducing the product too aggressively or early breaks the educational narrative and builds less trust.
cards.use_when: Restructuring a video ad script where the product pitch arrives too fast after the hook.

cards.title: Attack problem-agitation and objection handling, not just features
cards.summary: Sell benefits and resolve the viewer's real objections instead of listing ingredients and materials.
cards.use_when: Writing the body of a video ad or product-page copy where the audience needs to understand why the product works.

cards.title: Add dynamic editing to prevent drop-off on static talking heads
cards.summary: A long talking-head shot without overlays, B-roll or cuts becomes boring and viewers skip to a reel instead.
cards.use_when: Reviewing or editing a talking-head video ad that is underperforming on hold rate.

cards.title: Use a multi-persona call-out to widen the top of funnel
cards.summary: Calling out three related personas instead of one hooks more of the market while still qualifying the audience.
cards.use_when: Writing the opening line of a video ad for a broad-appeal product like a supplement.

cards.title: Don't shrink TAM with overly narrow brand positioning
cards.summary: Positioning a mass-market supplement toward elite athletes can cap scalability because the addressable market is too small and hard to reach.
cards.use_when: Deciding the target persona and positioning for a supplement or wellness product page and ad messaging.

cards.title: Define niche terms so credentials don't backfire
cards.summary: If you name a technical ingredient or condition, be precise; a knowledgeable audience will catch errors and lose trust.
cards.use_when: Writing product education for a specialized audience where incorrect terminology risks credibility.

cards.title: Edit out AI-scripting giveaways, especially contrast negation
cards.summary: The 'it's not X, it's Y' construction is a tell that a script was AI-written and should be avoided or rewritten.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a script drafted by an AI tool before producing a video or writing product page copy.

cards.title: Leverage a credible figure and a native setting for authenticity
cards.summary: A famous figure shot in a car, paired with trending terms, builds credibility and feels organic rather than like an ad.
cards.use_when: Planning a founder-led or celebrity-led video ad creative for a product or landing-page hero video.

cards.title: Reinforce relevance after naming a condition
cards.summary: Naming a clinical term is only useful if you immediately convince viewers they likely have it.
cards.use_when: Writing product education about a health problem or a technical product benefit that viewers don't already know they have.

cards.title: Structure a VSL's first 30-40 seconds as hook, problem, mechanism
cards.summary: A long-form video sales letter typically runs 3-4 minutes; the opening must hook the persona, agitate the problem, and introduce the mechanism before the product.
cards.use_when: Scripting the opening of a long-form VSL used on a landing page or as a paid social placement.

cards.title: Build a swipe file of competitor ad libraries for creative research
cards.summary: Watch the ad libraries of brands whose creatives are performing to study execution patterns you can adapt.
cards.use_when: Sourcing new ad angles, hooks or formats for your store's paid social creative pipeline.

cards.title: Diagnose underperformance by segmenting hook, bridge and body
cards.summary: When an ad underperforms, review the hook, the bridge and the body separately to locate the failure point.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting a video ad that has low conversion or low engagement after launch.

cards.title: Adapt hooks and education to the audience's awareness stage
cards.summary: The same product can be advertised at different awareness stages, but the level of education must match what the viewer already knows.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether a given ad should target problem-aware or solution-aware audiences in a Meta campaign.

cards.title: Meet the numbers you promise in ad claims and copy
cards.summary: Ad claims like 'clinical study' figures or 'up to X% off' must be accurate and verifiable or they damage credibility with engaged viewers.
cards.use_when: Finalizing claims, offers and supporting numbers for a video ad or product page.

cards.title: Clarity vs. Curiosity: Pick One, Never the Middle
cards.summary: Static ad copy must either be explicitly clear about the offer or deliberately vague enough to open a curiosity gap — ads that sit in the confusing middle fail.
cards.use_when: Writing or auditing the headline and primary text of a static ad for a cold-audience acquisition campaign.

cards.title: Design Static Ads Around the Eye's Reading Path
cards.summary: Structure a static so the eye moves through image, headline, explanation and proof in a deliberate sequence, closing the curiosity gap the image opened.
cards.use_when: Laying out a static ad image and deciding what element goes where to maximise cold-audience attention and comprehension.

cards.title: Treat Image and Headline Like a YouTube Thumbnail and Title
cards.summary: The image and headline must supply complementary context — each half-working alone is not enough to earn the click.
cards.use_when: Pairing a photo or illustration with a headline for a static ad, or diagnosing why a static is getting impressions but no clicks.

cards.title: Match Static Ad Format to Stage of Awareness
cards.summary: Most brands fail top-of-funnel by running product-aware or most-aware statics to cold, unaware audiences — instead lead cold traffic with education or problem agitation.
cards.use_when: Choosing which static ad concepts to produce for a cold prospecting campaign versus a retargeting campaign.

cards.title: Build Top-of-Funnel Statics Around Universal Problem Lists
cards.summary: A native-format static that names many common symptoms and maps each to an ingredient casts the widest possible net while staying contextually relevant to the target buyer.
cards.use_when: Designing a broad-reach cold-audience static for a supplement, wellness or consumable product where you need reach without wasted impressions.

cards.title: Rewrite Weak Benefit Headlines Into Persona-Specific Angles
cards.summary: A generic promise like 'guaranteed energy in 5 minutes' answers nothing a buyer is asking; rewrite it as a specific persona, problem or money-saving angle and test it across variants.
cards.use_when: Improving a static whose headline is a broad benefit claim and whose product is a commodity alternative (energy gum vs coffee, powder vs gummies).

cards.title: Use a Creator Handle Without the Creator to Reach a New Demographic
cards.summary: Running a static through a partner's handle while showing product rather than the influencer lets the ad reach a different gender or demographic than the creator's own audience.
cards.use_when: Planning a partnership or whitelisted static intended to expand the audience beyond the creator's core following.

cards.title: Test clear, non-graphic illustrations for sensitive product topics
cards.summary: Use illustrations to explain a relevant product problem without assuming the format guarantees approval or delivery.
cards.use_when: Producing static ad creative for a sensitive health, medical or appearance-related problem where a realistic photo would be graphic or policy-risky.

cards.title: Diagnose Confusing Statics: Graphs, Jargon and Slogans as Trust Killers
cards.summary: When a static's timeline, graph or slogan creates ambiguity rather than curiosity, readers disengage and the ad underdelivers regardless of budget.
cards.use_when: Auditing an underperforming static or an announcement-led ad (new formula, new version, relaunch) before spending further.

cards.title: Convert Complex Ingredient Claims to Plain-Language First
cards.summary: Lead with the everyday benefit and place the mechanistic or scientific explanation second, to expand the addressable audience without losing credibility.
cards.use_when: Writing supplement, health or technical product statics whose benefit bullets are full of mechanism-of-action terminology.

cards.title: Test Native and Novel Ad Formats for Arbitrage
cards.summary: Being early to a format the feed hasn't habituated to (tweet-style statics, partnership statics) creates a temporary attention advantage that decays once the format becomes common.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest creative production in a new static format before it becomes saturated in your category.

cards.title: Use Specific Numbers to Build Instant Authority (With Verification)
cards.summary: A precise statistic in a headline reads as scientific backing and raises perceived authority, but it must be substantiated before use.
cards.use_when: Writing a headline or proof line for a static where you need fast credibility on a cold audience.

cards.title: Problem-Agitate With a Persona and Problem in a Few Words
cards.summary: Naming a specific persona and a specific problem in the minimal number of words agitates the whole audience segment, not just those currently suffering it.
cards.use_when: Writing a top-of-funnel static headline for a niche product addressing a defined customer group or medication cohort.

cards.title: Route Curiosity Clicks to Advertorials, Not PDPs
cards.summary: When a static earns a click through a curiosity gap, sending the reader to a standard product display page wastes the click; an educational advertorial closes the gap first.
cards.use_when: Planning the destination URL for a cold-audience static whose headline or image deliberately withheld information.

cards.title: Launch Organic Content as Paid Without Rewriting for a CTA
cards.summary: Strong organic posts can be launched as ads unchanged; if the content is convincing the audience takes the next step without an explicit call to action.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adapt organic social posts into paid statics and whether a call to action is required.

cards.title: Compare static and video creative economics before allocating production
cards.summary: Lower static production costs may allow more tests; actual profitability depends on media cost and purchase outcomes.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate paid social creative budget and production capacity between static images and video for your store's ad account.

cards.title: The Clarity vs. Curiosity Spectrum for Static Ads
cards.summary: Static ads succeed when they are either explicitly clear about the offer or deliberately vague to open a curiosity gap — and fail when they sit ambiguously in the middle.
cards.use_when: Writing and designing a static ad concept and deciding whether to lead with the product/offer or with a curiosity-driven hook.

cards.title: Concept = Persona × Angle × Offer × Format
cards.summary: A true static ad concept is the intersection of persona, angle, offer and format; anything less is usually an immeasurable variation.
cards.use_when: Planning a static ad test batch for your store and deciding which changes count as new concepts versus minor design tweaks.

cards.title: Don't Start in Canva: Research and Concept Before Design
cards.summary: Build a static ad pipeline that front-loads deep consumer research and concepting, then executes in design tools — not the reverse.
cards.use_when: Setting up a repeatable static ad production process for your store or briefing a designer/creative strategist.

cards.title: Static Ad Formats and Where They Sit on the Spectrum
cards.summary: Catalog static ad formats — native statics, advertorials, before-and-afters, listicles, feature call-outs — and place each on the clarity-to-curiosity spectrum.
cards.use_when: Choosing which static ad format to produce for a given audience temperature or offer type in your paid social campaigns.

cards.title: Align Ad Concept to the Five Stages of Awareness
cards.summary: Use Eugene Schwartz's five stages of awareness (unaware, problem aware, solution aware, product aware, most aware) to match static ad concepts to the correct audience temperature.
cards.use_when: Mapping your store's static ad concepts to cold, warm, or retargeting audiences and diagnosing why a static ad underperforms.

cards.title: Route Curiosity Clicks to Educational Landing Pages, Not PDPs
cards.summary: Curiosity-driven top-of-funnel statics should send traffic to long-form educational pages (advertorials or quizzes), not standard product display pages.
cards.use_when: Deciding the destination URL for cold-traffic static ads and diagnosing poor conversion from curiosity hooks.

cards.title: Let Primary Text and Headline Carry the Education Burden
cards.summary: The primary text and headline must convey what a static image cannot, since the image alone is limited in how much it can teach or persuade.
cards.use_when: Writing the copy that accompanies a static ad image in your paid social campaigns.

cards.title: Forecast Creative Volume with Churn and Revenue Formulas
cards.summary: Plan static ad production output by using formulas based on churn percentage and average revenue per ad to size the volume you actually need.
cards.use_when: Sizing the weekly or monthly static ad production capacity your store's paid social account requires.

cards.title: Static Ads as the Cheapest Creative Testing Ground
cards.summary: Statics cost far less to produce and serve than video, making them the fastest, cheapest way to test new angles, offers and personas before investing in video production.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to allocate creative production budget for testing new product angles, offers or personas in a paid social account.

cards.title: Clarity vs Curiosity: Never Sit in the Middle
cards.summary: Static ads must be either maximally clear about the offer or deliberately curiosity-driven; ads that mix both fail as undifferentiated 'slop' and get stuck as mid-funnel attribution-scoopers.
cards.use_when: Reviewing or briefing a static ad creative to decide whether its messaging direction is decisive enough to perform on cold audiences.

cards.title: Avoid Last-Click Attribution on Top-of-Funnel Statics
cards.summary: Top-of-funnel static ads drive cheap clicks and halo conversions that retargeting ads claim under last-click attribution, so judging them by in-platform ROAS alone wrongly kills them.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to scale or kill top-of-funnel static ads, or setting up creative reporting that reflects true business contribution.

cards.title: Concept = Persona × Angle × Offer (not design)
cards.summary: A true creative concept changes the persona, angle or offer; design tweaks and format swaps alone are just variations and do not broaden reach.
cards.use_when: Briefing a creative team or reviewing submitted statics to confirm whether they represent genuinely new concepts or just cosmetic variations.

cards.title: Ad Volume Forecasting: Churn Back-Propagation
cards.summary: Back-calculate required static ad volume from how fast winning ads churn and your historical hit rate, rather than testing as much as possible.
cards.use_when: Planning monthly creative output or deciding how many new static ads to produce to sustain paid social performance.

cards.title: Prioritize Research Over Concepting Over Production
cards.summary: The static ad production pipeline is research → concepting → build → variations → feedback, and quality collapses if you skip straight to design tools like Canva.
cards.use_when: Structuring a static ad production workflow or diagnosing why existing statics underperform despite good design.

cards.title: Creative Variation: Change One Concept Element, Not the Pixel
cards.summary: Because Meta's Andromeda groups near-identical ads, tiny design changes have no measurable uplift; variations should change persona, offer or angle while keeping the winning format.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to change when scaling a winning static format, or rejecting a designer's background-color variations.

cards.title: Expected Gross Profit Per Ad: The Real Comparison Metric
cards.summary: Compare creative types by expected gross profit after production cost (revenue per ad minus ad spend minus production cost), not by headline ROAS alone.
cards.use_when: Choosing between producing more statics or more videos in a paid social budget, or justifying a static-heavy creative plan.

cards.title: Stages of Awareness Applied to Static Ads
cards.summary: Static ads tend to sit low in the stages of awareness; to scale them you must deliberately build statics for higher awareness stages and use primary text plus landing pages to bridge the gap.
cards.use_when: Choosing what awareness level a new static ad should target, especially when trying to reach cold audiences instead of retargeting buyers.

cards.title: Design the Visual Hierarchy on Three Levers
cards.summary: Control how a viewer's eye moves through a static using sizing, contrast and whitespace so the first fixation lands on the highest-awareness element.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a static ad layout, or briefing a designer on how the eye should travel through the creative.

cards.title: Treat Primary Text and Headline as Core, Not Decoration
cards.summary: On statics, headlines and primary text get far more consumption than on video, so build a YouTube-thumbnail-style curiosity pairing between image and text.
cards.use_when: Writing the copy that accompanies a static ad image, or reviewing primary text in a static ad breakdown.

cards.title: Native vs Non-Native Scroll-Stop Levers
cards.summary: Statics stop the scroll either by feeling native to the platform or by being deliberately non-native and clickbaity; each direction dictates where the message and selling live.
cards.use_when: Deciding the creative direction (native organic-feel vs. obvious ad) for a new static before starting design.

cards.title: Whitelisting/Native Static with Long-Form Copy (IM8 Example)
cards.summary: A tweet-style static run from a personality profile, agitating a very wide symptom list and educating on solutions, can reach cold audiences without looking like an ad.
cards.use_when: Planning a native or whitelisting-style static around a broad symptom/problem list for a supplement or wellness product.

cards.title: Long-Copy Story Static for Older/Problem-Aware Audiences
cards.summary: A plain, organic-looking story post with a long narrative about a personal problem can pull a wide audience and disqualify non-relevant viewers through its content.
cards.use_when: Writing a static ad aimed at an older or problem-aware audience (e.g., menopause, hormonal issues) that needs trust built through story.

cards.title: How Design Quality Conveys or Destroys Authority
cards.summary: Design alone does not sell, but bad spacing and off-center product shots can erase the authority that specificity and positioning build.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a finished static for layout quality before it goes live, or deciding whether to fix design versus rewrite copy.

cards.title: Match Image and Copy at the Same Awareness Stage
cards.summary: When the static image assumes one awareness stage and the copy speaks to another, the ad fails; the image and copy must sit at the same stage.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing static ad that is underperforming, or QA review before launch.

cards.title: Rotate Concept Elements to Scale a Winning Format
cards.summary: Once a static format proves out, scale it by substituting a concept element (persona, offer or angle) rather than iterating on the format itself.
cards.use_when: Planning the next batch of statics after a format like problem-agitation or native advertorial has proven to work.

cards.title: Format-to-Awareness Map for Static Ad Planning
cards.summary: Use a rough map of static formats by funnel stage to decide which formats to test at the top, middle and bottom of the funnel.
cards.use_when: Building a static ad test plan across funnel stages or filling gaps in a creative testing calendar.

cards.title: Diagnosing a Static's Curiosity Direction (Caffeine Gum Example)
cards.summary: A static that sits in the middle—vague enough to be interesting but lacking specificity to sell or clear curiosity—fails at both, and should be pushed to one pole.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a static headline that feels neither clearly persuasive nor deliberately mysterious, or reviewing a static driving to a plain product page.

cards.title: AI-Assisted Static Production with Human Checkpoints
cards.summary: AI can be used at every stage of static production, but automating everything produces slop; keep human intervention at research or concepting, or make the build human.
cards.use_when: Designing an AI-assisted static ad production pipeline for a store that wants volume without losing creative quality.

cards.title: Curiosity vs. Education: Pick One Lane in Static Ads
cards.summary: Static ads fail when they split between a curiosity hook and a product education pitch instead of committing fully to one.
cards.use_when: Deciding the strategic posture for a new static ad promoting a product launch, reformulation, or new SKU.

cards.title: Advertorial Static Funnel with Ranked Product Roundup
cards.summary: A doctor-authored 'best products of the year' static that feeds a ranked review page and quiz funnel converts because it educates before selling.
cards.use_when: Building a paid social static and landing page for a supplement or considered-purchase product where education is needed before the buy.

cards.title: Read-Order Design: Make the Eye Sequence Tell the Story
cards.summary: Design static ads so the viewer's natural reading path moves from hook to context to proof to purchase-intent without dead ends.
cards.use_when: Laying out a static ad where you must sequence product imagery, headline, supporting claims and social proof.

cards.title: Product Shot on Static: Add Purchase Friction Deliberately
cards.summary: Including a plain product shot on a premium static can intentionally reduce sticker shock at the landing page, even if it lowers visual polish.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to show the physical product (tub, bottle, box) on a static ad versus keeping only lifestyle imagery.

cards.title: Native Static for Top-of-Funnel Attention and Retargeting
cards.summary: A paparazzi-style native static disrupts the feed by disguising the ad as organic content, feeding awareness and retargeting rather than direct sales.
cards.use_when: Planning top-of-funnel paid social when you need cheap attention and a retargeting pool rather than immediate conversion.

cards.title: Persona Callout Static for Problem-Aware Audiences (GLP-1 Template)
cards.summary: Lead a static with a specific persona label and recognizable object, then widen into a curiosity gap about a solution rather than naming the product.
cards.use_when: Writing a static ad targeting a clearly defined, problem-aware audience segment where a specific identifier is instantly recognizable.

cards.title: Match Static Ad Type to Landing Page Depth
cards.summary: A static's conversion performance depends on matching its level of education to the depth of the landing page it feeds.
cards.use_when: Choosing the landing page destination for a new static ad, or diagnosing why a static isn't converting.

cards.title: Use Social Proof with Visible Credibility on Statics
cards.summary: A review callout only converts if the viewer instantly recognizes it as a credible review — add stars, names or faces.
cards.use_when: Placing testimonials or review quotes inside a static ad or on the PDP hero.

cards.title: Brand Logo Can Mask Weak Static Creative
cards.summary: Well-known brands can coast on logo recognition, hiding bad static creative that would fail for smaller advertisers.
cards.use_when: Benchmarking competitor statics or assessing your own creative honesty versus brand equity.

cards.title: Zero-follower whatnot launch: sell one item, no promotion buildup
cards.summary: Launch a live-selling account by scheduling a same-day 15-minute show to sell a single low-friction item rather than over-prepared marathons.
cards.use_when: Planning your first live-selling show on Whatnot (or a similar live auction platform) with few or no followers.

cards.title: Sell to resellers when you have no audience
cards.summary: Price items so a reseller can still profit, because during a cold start the reliable buyer is another reseller, not the end consumer.
cards.use_when: Choosing pricing and target buyer for your first live-selling shows before you have a regular audience.

cards.title: Curate impulse-purchase inventory over niche high-specificity items
cards.summary: Choose broad-appeal, low-price, impulse-friendly products rather than items requiring a very specific buyer to be present.
cards.use_when: Selecting which products to source and list for a live-selling show.

cards.title: Run a fast auction cadence (5-second bids, low starts)
cards.summary: Top live sellers run auctions in seconds at low opening prices, which converts browsing traffic into fast impulse purchases.
cards.use_when: Setting auction duration and starting price for items in a live-selling show.

cards.title: Entertain to retain: the longer they watch, the more they buy
cards.summary: Live selling has a social/entertainment layer; keeping viewers engaged longer increases purchase likelihood, so add a personality hook to the show.
cards.use_when: Designing the format and on-camera persona for a live-selling show to raise session length.

cards.title: Remove the awkwardness of a solo first stream
cards.summary: The hardest part of a first live show is talking to an empty room; expect it and treat 'fake it till you make it' as the way through.
cards.use_when: Preparing mentally and practically for your first live-selling broadcast with no viewers.
